solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pole has millions invested in bank

indicators.note: invested in means put inside, so the millions go into the pole

parts.note: a caber is the pole tossed at Highland games

explanation.surface: A Pole has put millions of his money into a bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' with its capital looks like a Polish person; it is the caber, the tree trunk thrown at Scottish Highland games.
explanation.definitionFit: A camber is the sloping tilt of a road surface, a kind of bank on a bend.

clue.text: Fury of a college teacher being cut short

indicators.note: cut short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a lector is a reader or lecturer at a college

explanation.surface: The rage of a college lecturer whose job was cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fury' looks like anger, but with its capital it is one of the three Furies of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Alecto is one of the three Erinyes, the avenging goddesses of Greek mythology.

clue.text: I'm not the person who will have this meat well done!

definitions.text: I'm not the person who will have this meat well done!

parts.words: I'm not the person who will have this meat well done!
parts.note: bully is tinned corned beef, so the speaker hands that meat to someone else, and the whole phrase is also a sarcastic 'well done!'

explanation.walkthrough: Bully beef is corned beef; the phrase, read as meat offered to you rather than me, is also an old exclamation of grudging congratulation.
explanation.definitionFit: The expression is a mocking or ironic form of congratulation, like saying good for you.

clue.text: Speed over old city carrying prisoner who has a tale to tell?

definitions.text: who has a tale to tell?

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above
carrying means holding the prisoner inside

parts.note: rate means speed
a con is a convict
Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A fast vehicle heading to an ancient city with a prisoner who has a story.
explanation.definitionFit: A raconteur is a skilled storyteller who entertains with anecdotes.

clue.text: Arrive with noise to welcome in ace entertainer

parts.note: to arrive is to come

indicators.note: to welcome in means the noise takes the ace inside itself

parts.note: din is a loud noise
A is the card abbreviation for ace

explanation.surface: Someone turns up noisily to greet a star performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedian is a stage performer who makes audiences laugh, a type of entertainer.

clue.text: Old books firm cuts into small pieces

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
to dice is to chop into small cubes

explanation.surface: A company shredding ancient volumes.
explanation.definitionFit: Codices are ancient manuscripts bound in book form, the plural of codex.

clue.text: Doctor, a gloomy type

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
per means a, as in once a day

explanation.surface: A doctor who is a miserable sort.
explanation.definitionFit: A moper is someone who sulks and is listless and dejected.

clue.text: Operator was first to get up

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means reading from the bottom upwards

parts.note: led means was in front, was first

explanation.surface: A worker who was the first to rise in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: Del is the mathematical operator written as an inverted triangle, also called nabla.
explanation.definitionFit: In vector calculus, del is the differential symbol used for gradient, divergence and curl.

clue.text: Sick English among workers in overseas islands

indicators.note: among means placed within the workers

parts.note: ants are crossword workers, from worker ants
ill means sick

explanation.surface: A sick Englishman among labourers on far-flung islands.
explanation.definitionFit: The Antilles are the island chain of the Caribbean, far across the sea from Britain.

clue.text: Substituted one material with another — hint of decay?

parts.note: rep is a ribbed woven fabric
lace is another fabric

indicators.note: a hint of a word is just its opening letter, here of decay

parts.note: first letter of decay

explanation.surface: Swapping one fabric for another, perhaps because the first was rotting.
explanation.walkthrough: Rep is a corded fabric used for upholstery; the surface reads as a whole definition but only 'Substituted' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: To replace something is to put a substitute in its position.

clue.text: One who famously tried being holy, no longer with us

parts.note: pi is informal for pious or holy
the late person is one who has died

explanation.surface: A famous trial figure being pious and now dead.
explanation.walkthrough: Pontius Pilate presided over the trial of Jesus; 'tried' means put on trial, not attempted.
explanation.definitionFit: Pontius Pilate was the Roman governor who judged Jesus at his trial.

clue.text: Stone that covers a stick

indicators.note: covers means the outer letters go around the A

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the weight
yon is an old word for that, as in yon hill

explanation.surface: A stone sitting on top of a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay on is to remain attached, which is to stick to something.

clue.text: Holiday destination with a hundred men gathered by northern boundary

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
OR, other ranks, means soldiers who are not officers
a wall is a boundary

explanation.surface: A holiday spot where a hundred men gather by a northern wall.
explanation.walkthrough: CORNWALL is England's south-western county, a popular holiday area; OR (other ranks) is the crossword stock for men.
explanation.definitionFit: The county is famous for seaside tourism, making it a common vacation spot.

clue.text: Caught out as an Oxford type misplaced?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: surprised or put at a disadvantage
second meaning: an Oxford is a style of shoe

explanation.walkthrough: 'Oxford type' suggests a university man, but an Oxford is a lace-up shoe; put it on the wrong foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Being wrong-footed means being caught off balance by something unexpected.

clue.text: Maybe maiden beginning to smile got ring and married veiled?

parts.note: a maiden is one example of an over in cricket, one with no runs scored

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, here of smile

parts.note: first letter of smile
had means got
O is ring-shaped
wed means married

explanation.surface: A young bride starts smiling, gets her ring and marries under a veil.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a maiden is an over of six balls in which no runs are scored, hence 'Maybe'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overshadowed is obscured or hidden, much as a veil conceals; the question mark flags the loose fit.

clue.text: Lamenting changes, getting into a row

indicators.note: changes means the letters of lamenting are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone bewailing changes and ending up in a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting into a row' looks like starting a quarrel; here the row is a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Alignment is arrangement in a straight line, such as soldiers forming a line.

clue.text: It's different, being under informal head? Not something to worry about!

indicators.note: in a down clue, being under means placed below

parts.note: nob is slang for the head
other means different

explanation.surface: Someone unusual working under a casual boss shrugs off any worries.
explanation.definitionFit: No bother is an informal reassurance that something is no trouble at all.

clue.text: Pink York gent out horse-riding

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man from York dressed in pink out riding to hounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Hunting coats are traditionally called pink, which explains the colour in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Pony trekking is cross-country travel on ponies, a form of horseback riding.

clue.text: Hide from child's family

parts.note: kid's means child's
kin means family

explanation.surface: Keeping something secret from a child's relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb, but it is the noun meaning animal skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Kidskin is leather made from a young goat's skin, so a kind of hide.

clue.text: Old monarch, kind to be on top

indicators.note: in a down clue, on top means placed above the monarch

parts.note: form means kind or type
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: An old king, kindly disposed to rule.
explanation.definitionFit: Former means earlier or previous, describing what used to be.

clue.text: Female, old and obstinate, making concentrated effort

parts.note: cussed means stubborn or obstinate

explanation.surface: A stubborn old woman putting all her energy into a task.
explanation.definitionFit: Being focussed means directing one's attention intently on a single task.

clue.text: Proud walk of good person — something groovy

parts.note: ST is a saint, a good person
a rut is a groove

explanation.surface: A saintly person walking proudly and looking cool.
explanation.definitionFit: To strut is to walk with a stiff, swaggering gait.

clue.text: One violently against right-winger

indicators.note: violently suggests the letters of one are thrown about

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: Someone fiercely opposed to a right-wing politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A neocon, short for neoconservative, is a hawkish American conservative.

clue.text: Sounder of warning up to now about hospital

indicators.note: about means placed around the hospital letter

parts.note: so far means up to now
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: The alarm has so far been raised about the hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: A shofar is the ram's-horn trumpet of Jewish ritual, once blown as an alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: The ram's horn was blown to signal danger or to summon people, so it sounds alarms.

clue.text: Tiresome job that's unhealthy

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a chore, a tedious task
second meaning: British slang for a cigarette

explanation.walkthrough: Fag is British slang for both a chore and a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a wearying task and a cigarette, known to damage health.

clue.text: Be in step in fortress when confronting the enemy

indicators.note: confronting means facing, so the fortress stands in front of the enemy

parts.note: a keep is the stronghold of a castle
time is the enemy, from the saying

explanation.surface: Marching in step inside a castle while facing the foe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time is the enemy' is a crossword favourite for TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep time is to move in rhythm with a beat, as marchers do.

clue.text: Reportedly cheer up seaside resort

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the town sounds like the verb

parts.note: to brighten is to cheer up

explanation.surface: A seaside town said to lift the spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: Brighton is a resort town on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Brighton is a well-known holiday town on the English Channel coast.

clue.text: Union with Diana in royal family

parts.note: TU is the abbreviation for trade union
Diana Dors was a British film actress of the 1950s

explanation.surface: A marriage that brings Diana into the royal family.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Princess Diana marrying into the Windsors; the Diana wanted is the actress Diana Dors.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudors were the dynasty ruling England from Henry VII to Elizabeth I.
